# VitalityRise — Men's Pelvic Floor Training

VitalityRise (App Store name: Vitality Rise: Men's Health) is an iPhone app for men's pelvic floor training. It runs guided contract-and-relax sessions, pelvic mobility and breathing work, a 30-day plan, and progress scoring. Everything a user enters stays on the device: no account, no cloud sync, no ads. Built by Kyrylo Lozovyi (VITALITY RISE LLC). US pricing: $4.99/week, $9.99/month or $34.99/year (both with a 3-day free trial), or $99.99 once. iOS 17 or later.

It is a general wellness app, not medical care, and does not diagnose or treat erectile dysfunction or any other condition.

## Pages

- [Pelvic floor training for men, done properly](https://www.vitalityrize.me/): A guided pelvic floor trainer for men: timed contract-and-relax sessions, breathing and mobility work, a 30-day plan. Your answers stay on your device.
- [Who builds VitalityRise](https://www.vitalityrize.me/about/): VitalityRise is built by one developer, Kyrylo Lozovyi, trading as VITALITY RISE LLC. No investors, no medical board — and rules the app will not break.
- [Kegel apps for men, compared](https://www.vitalityrize.me/best-kegel-apps-for-men/): Dr. Kegel, Kegel Men, Better P, Kegel Trainer and VitalityRise: what each costs on the App Store and which to pick. Disclosure — we make one of them.
- [Erectile dysfunction without medication](https://www.vitalityrize.me/erectile-dysfunction-without-medication/): Aerobic exercise, weight, sleep, smoking, alcohol and pelvic floor training, ranked by the evidence behind each — plus what does not work.
- [Kegel exercises for men](https://www.vitalityrize.me/kegel-exercises-for-men/): How to find the muscle, the squeeze-and-release protocol used in the trials, how many reps, and the four mistakes that make the whole thing useless.
- [How the programme was built](https://www.vitalityrize.me/methodology/): The sources behind the 30-day plan — the pelvic floor trials, the physical activity reviews, the session timings — and what we deliberately left out.
- [Pelvic floor exercises and erectile dysfunction](https://www.vitalityrize.me/pelvic-floor-exercises-erectile-dysfunction/): The randomised trial numbers: 40% of men regained normal erectile function at six months, 35.5% improved, 24.5% did not. Plus the mechanism and the limits.
- [Pelvic floor self-check](https://www.vitalityrize.me/pelvic-floor-self-check/): Eight questions that sort your symptoms into a weak pelvic floor, an over-tight one, or see-a-doctor. Runs in your browser; nothing is stored or sent.
- [Exercises for premature ejaculation](https://www.vitalityrize.me/premature-ejaculation-exercises/): A 12-week programme took 40 men with lifelong premature ejaculation from 31.7 seconds to 146.2. What the study proved, what it did not, and the protocol.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.vitalityrize.me/privacy/): What VitalityRise stores on your device, what it never uploads, the anonymous analytics it does send, and how to erase everything.
